title: Predictive Geo-Eviction & Signal-Fusion Routing for Capacity-Aware Latency SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a predictive, signal-fusion routing controller that combines latency SLO signals, per-region capacity forecasts, and geo-affinity preferences to make per-request routing decisions. Goal: keep tail latency < 200ms P95 for hosted customers while avoiding cross-region over-provisioning and reducing failed requests during regional capacity pressure. The system should integrate with existing circuit-breaker and load-shedding primitives and provide a controlled canary rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Service correctly weights candidate regions by predicted SLO attainment probability and available capacity for 90% of requests in synthetic workload tests.
When a region's capacity forecast drops below 20% of baseline, controller triggers graceful geo-eviction for low-priority tenants without violating P95 SLOs for high-priority tenants.
Circuit breakers trip and recover according to new adaptive thresholds (see design decisions) and are observable in runtime dashboards.
End-to-end canary rollout demonstrates zero-severity customer-facing errors and <2% increase in average token latency compared to baseline for test traffic segment.
design_decisions: Use a short-horizon predictive model (30s-5min) combining per-AZ CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, recent P95 latencies, and request mix to estimate region capacity headroom.
Signal fusion: normalize metrics into a unified score (0-1) and apply a tunable bias for geo pinning. Default bias keeps 85% of user sessions in their home-region when headroom >= 40%.
Routing algorithm: weighted softmax over candidate region scores with temperature parameter that is traffic-class configurable (low temperature => stickiness; high => aggressive failover).
Load shedding: move from binary shed to progressive degradation — reduce batch size or enable KV cache reuse, then circuit-break to fallback model variants, and finally reject low-priority requests.
Circuit-breaker thresholds are adaptive: they use EWMA of failure/latency signals and a hysteresis window to avoid flapping during transient spikes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests against runtime simulator (local).
Phase 1: Internal dogfood rollout to platform-team only with 1% traffic and synthetic region failures enabled. Monitor SLOs and dashboards for 48h.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 10% over 4 hours with automatic rollback on >3 SLO breaches in 1h window.
Phase 3: Apply to all hosted traffic with tiered defaults and ability for customers to opt into strict geo-pinning.
metrics: P95 latency (global and per-region) - primary SLO
Request success rate (5xx and model errors) - target >= 99.9%
Regional capacity headroom estimate - modeled metric
Circuit-breaker trip rate and recovery time
Cross-region egress bandwidth and cost delta
test_plan: Create a runtime simulator that replays historical traffic traces into multi-region topology and validates decision outcomes.
Synthetic overload tests: inject CPU/GPU contention and spike queue depth in a single region to verify geo-eviction and failover behavior.
Chaos tests: scheduled region partition + delayed KV cache responses to validate hysteresis and non-flapping of circuit breakers.
A/B canary comparing existing steering -> new controller for latency, errors, and cost metrics over 72h.
